Let me redo this properly with a simpler approach: build rc with 3 frame offsets by appending rc(segments). For reverse strand, coordinate mapping: for frame with shift k on the reverse-complement string (rv), the codon occupying rv positions p..p+2 corresponds to forward positions N-p-2..N-p-1 (0-based). So a codon at rv index i (0-based, in the frame string rv shifting won't work directly; better to use rv_full = rc(seq) and consider codons starting at position start_i = i where i = k + 3n).

Let me define: rv_full = rc(seq), length N. Codons of frame k (k in 0,1,2): positions i = k, k+3, k+6, ... A codon at rows i..i+2 in rv_full corresponds to forward (0-based) N-1-i down to N-3-i, i.e. forward interval [N-3-i, N-1-i] inclusive, with codon base1 = forward position N-1-i.

For an ORF from rv codon index a (first ATG) to stop codon at rv index b (inclusive), the forward coordinates: start (ATG first base) = N-1-(a_start position). For codon at rv position i = k+3a: forward first base index = N-1-i. For the stop codon last base at rv position j = k+3b+2: forward index = N-1-j. So forward ORF interval (0-based inclusive): [N-1-(k+3b+2), N-1-(k+3a)].

That's much simpler than my earlier mess. Same for forward: codon i = shift+3a; forward ORF: [shift+3a, shift+3(b)+2], where b is stop codon index; if no stop codon and b = len(cods)-1... careful.
